en: The Section on Detailed Exposition, Chapter Four: Convergence (Sampāta)
The Conveying of the Footings (Padaṭṭhāna-hārasampāta). In this context, what is the Conveying of the Footings?
It is the verse: “Therefore, for one whose mind is guarded, the range is right intention.”
“Therefore, for one whose mind is guarded”: this is the foundation for the three types of good conduct.
“Having right intention as his range”: this is the foundation for serenity (*samatha*).
“Having right view as his priority”: this is the foundation for insight (*vipassanā*).
“Having known arising and passing away” is the proximate cause for the plane of vision.
“The bhikkhu who has overcome sloth and torpor” is the proximate cause for energy.
“He abandons all states of woe” is the proximate cause for development.
The section on the application of the modes of conveyance and their foundations is concluded.
